OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepts spaces, dashes and
            brackets and an optional leading '+' with country code; stored and
            returned in E.164 form (a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits). When no
            country code is given, '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Acknowledgement that this owner deliberately shares a household with an
            existing owner. When true, the create request is allowed even though
            another owner has the same last name and address; otherwise such a
            request is rejected as a conflict. Not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of the first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The canonical region derived from the owner's city via the pinned city-to-region
                table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' for any other city.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is the
                upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a global
                4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned when the owner is created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is
                the last two digits of the registration date's year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by owners that deliberately share a household
                (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner is created with
                'sharesHousehold' true; the joining owner and the existing household
                members all carry the same value. Absent for owners not in a shared household.
              type: string
              example: 'H-3F9A1C2B4D5E'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that already shared this owner's first and last name
                (compared case-insensitively) at the moment this owner was created. Zero when the
                name was new.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's membership level, a number from 1 to 3 fixed when the owner was
                created. It starts at 1, gains 1 when an email address is present, and gains 1
                when the owner has a unique name (namesakeCount is zero), capped at 3. Level 4 is
                reserved for tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners had already been registered on this owner's
                (business-day-adjusted) registration date at the moment it was created;
                false otherwise.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel, derived from their details: 'EMAIL'
                when an email address is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              enum:
                - EMAIL
                - PHONE
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets

      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object

        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.

The implementation is complete and the full test suite is green. Here's what I did.

## Summary

Consolidated the three separate duplicate checks (telephone, email, household) into a single derived `identityKey` = `normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + householdId`. A create request is now rejected with 409 only when the whole key exactly matches an existing owner's.

### New code
- **`IdentityKey`** (helper, in `rest/function/owner`) — the one place the key is derived. `of(telephone, email, householdId)` normalizes each part by reusing the existing `TelephoneNormalizer` (E.164) and `EmailNormalizer` (lower-case, empty when absent); `forOwner(Owner)` reads the parts off an owner. Single source of truth for both the check and the response.
- **`EnsureUniqueIdentity`** (pipeline step) — computes the built owner's key and rejects an exact full-key match against existing owners via a checked `DuplicateIdentityException` (409). It runs **after `AssignHousehold`**, because the household part of the key is the assigned household id, so the built owner carries its final key parts before the check.
- **`DuplicateIdentityException`** + handler + `officefloor/escalation/…DuplicateIdentityException.yml` (409, mirroring the existing handlers).

### Behaviour change realized
Because telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same `householdId`) with different telephones now have different keys and are both allowed — only an exact full-key match is a duplicate. The acceptance test (`coreRejectsIdentityCollision`) confirms two lone owners (both with empty email and empty household id) sharing a telephone collide.

### Wiring & response
- `owners.POST.yml`: removed `ensureUniqueTelephone` / `ensureUniqueHousehold` / `ensureUniqueEmail`; inserted `ensureUniqueIdentity` after `assignHousehold` (governed by the transaction). Normalization/format-validation steps stayed.
- `openapi.yml`: added the read-only `identityKey` field to the `Owner` schema, and `OwnerMapper` derives it (like the other computed fields) so every owner response returns it.

### Cleanup
Deleted the three obsolete `EnsureUnique*` functions, their three `Duplicate*Exception`/handler pairs and escalation YAMLs, and updated the dangling javadoc references in `TelephoneNormalizer`, `EmailNormalizer`, `HouseholdNormalizer`, `AssignHousehold`, `NormalizeAddress`, and `CountHousehold`.

`./mvnw test` → `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (the only test class), BUILD SUCCESS.

One thing worth flagging: this removes household uniqueness for owners who don't set `sharesHousehold` — previously same-lastname+address was a 409 regardless of phone; now, since lone owners keep a null household id, two such owners with different phones both succeed. That's the intended consequence of the spec ("only an exact full-key match is a duplicate"), but it does mean `sharesHousehold` no longer gates anything at the check (it still controls whether the shared household id is stamped).
